result:
The video is rendered to `studio/final.mp4`. It is 1080×1350 at 30 fps, 9.0 s long (270 frames), and the render took 23.8 s.

`npx hyperframes check` passed with no findings: lint, runtime, motion and layout were all clean, and contrast passed 74 of 74 text checks. I didn't look at any frames, and the "Snapshots" step of the check was disabled, so the layout was only checked by the tool.

The six panels light up in order, 1.5 s each. The output file name appears under the lit panel: spec.md, data.json, story.md, index.html, timing.json, final.mp4. The last panel (Ship) stays lit to the end.

I wrote `spec.md`, `data.json`, `story.md` and `timing.json` before building the animation. The windows in `timing.json` match the `data-start` and `data-duration` values in `index.html`.

I also added a "1.5 s per panel · 9 s" line under the title. `data.json` lists every number on screen with its source: the 6 in the title, panel numbers 01–06, 1.5 s and 9 s.

The render also printed a pointer to the HyperFrames desktop app, where you can keep editing by chatting with its assistant, Framey: https://hyperframes.dev/studio/download?os=linux
